Brazil's right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro speaks after his election loss on October 25 [Pablo Porciuncula/AFP]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and ReutersPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
The political party of Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has acknowledged the result of Brazil’s presidential run-off, despite the right-wing candidate pledging to annul the outcome.
On Monday, Valdemar Costa Neto, the leader of the right-wing Liberal Party, issued a statement saying his political group had accepted the outcome of the vote.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Lula holds off far right with victory in Brazil presidential electionlist 2 of 3World reacts to Lula’s victory in Brazil’s presidential electionlist 3 of 3Brazil election results 2026: Key takeaways from Lula’s historic winend of list
Still, he echoed Bolsonaro’s concerns about the circumstances surrounding the election.
“We recognise the presidential election results,” Costa Neto said. “But we believe the issues raised need to be properly clarified.”
On Sunday, Bolsonaro was defeated by left-wing incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva by a margin of more than 4.4 million votes.
Bolsonaro has yet to formally concede. In a post-election speech, he called the election results “unacceptable”, citing a last-minute extension to voting hours.
“We will take legal action,” he told supporters. “I will request that these elections be annulled.”
An extension to Sunday’s vote had been sought by the campaigns of both candidates — but for different reasons.
Bolsonaro’s camp had pointed to inclement weather that impeded some voters from reaching polling stations. Parts of southern Brazil, considered a right-wing stronghold, had experienced heavy rains on Sunday.

President Donald Trump has expressed scepticism about the integrity of California's mail-in voting system [Mike Blake/Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
A United States appeals court has ruled against the administration of President Donald Trump in its bid to block the state of California from counting certain mail-in ballots this election cycle.
In a decision on Monday, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request from the government to sequester roughly 20,000 mailed ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm election.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3US appeals court sceptical of Trump’s lawsuit over California voter rollslist 2 of 3All you need to know about US midterms 2026list 3 of 3US judge blocks federal operations seeking to identify non-citizen votersend of list
The Trump administration had asserted that the ballots were sent to people who are “likely” non-citizens.
But it has not publicly revealed how it created its list or determined that the voters identified upon it were ineligible due to their citizenship status.
In a two-to-one decision, the appeals court said the Trump administration had not given lower courts enough time to review the case. It therefore declined to stop California’s ballot tabulation.
The court’s majority also underscored that election administration was the state’s responsibility under the US Constitution.
The Trump administration was asking “the federal court to dictate to a state legislature a matter squarely within the state’s traditional domain”, Judge Gabriel Sanchez wrote in his opinion.
Sanchez also warned that granting the Trump administration’s petition would be “inviting disorder and confusion for voters and election officials alike”.

Exterior view of the Consulate General of the Russian Federation in Constanta, Romania [File: Costin Dinca/ Inquam Photos]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and ReutersPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
Romanian authorities say they have uncovered a network “coordinated” by Russia that they believe was responsible for a fire at an industrial site near a state-owned weapons factory in September.
Romania’s Intelligence Service said on Monday that the blaze in the central city of Brasov on September 14 was “part of a wider campaign of sabotage operations coordinated” by Russia amid its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The agency said the operations were aimed at arms manufacturers and “other targets of military and industrial interest”.
“These actions are intended to intimidate, undermine defence capabilities and weaken the contribution of the targeted states to European and regional security,” it said in a statement.
There was no immediate comment from Russia on Romania’s claim. Moscow has previously repeatedly denied such accusations.
Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, known as DIICOT, said three people had been involved in the Brasov fire – two Belarusians and a Ukrainian, all living in European Union countries.
Two were “tracked down and remanded in custody in Germany while they were preparing to commit similar offenses”, the directorate said.
The third remains at large in Poland.

Jordan attacks Syria in response to Karak church attackBy Al Jazeera Staff and APPublished On 26 Oct 202626 Oct 2026
Jordan has carried out air strikes in Syria in “retaliation” for last week’s deadly church attack, with Syrian authorities saying the raids killed at least seven people, including three children and a woman.
The attacks on Monday prompted Syria to close its main crossing with Jordan.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Suwayda remains in stasis as US signals differences with Israel on Syrialist 2 of 3Jordan arrests three suspects over church attack in dawn raid: What to knowlist 3 of 3Jordan arrests three suspects over deadly church attackend of list
Jordan’s Armed Forces said in a statement that it targeted “hideouts” of armed groups in southeastern Syria in response to the gun attack at a church in its Karak governorate on Friday. At least nine people were killed and dozens more wounded in the shootings.
The Jordanian military said the strikes on Syria were launched “in coordination with the Syrian government”.
It said the raids “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”.
Syria, however, denied any coordination with Jordan.
In a statement, the Syrian government said “the military operation was conducted without prior coordination or notification” and said it has launched an investigation.
Syria’s Civil Defence service said at least four sites in rural Deraa and Suweyda provinces were hit on Monday evening, and that its crews had recovered the bodies of seven people: three men, a woman and three children.

Bayern Munich's Harry Kane celebrates after winning the men's Ballon d'Or award [Matthew Childs/Action Images via Reuters]By ReutersPublished On 26 Oct 202626 Oct 2026
Harry Kane has completed ‌his long quest for football’s highest individual honour, with the Bayern Munich and England striker winning the Ballon ⁠d’Or after a record-breaking season ⁠that cemented his status as one of the game’s greatest goalscorers.
Kane is the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won it in 2001.
“Wow, wow, wow!” Kane said after taking ⁠the stage on Monday. “I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.
“Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations ⁠to all the winners and nominees tonight, and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve.”
Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or Feminin for the third time.
Kane’s move to Bayern in 2023 brought the team trophies that had long eluded him. In 2025-26, he coupled that success with goalscoring numbers that made him the leading Ballon d’Or candidate.
The England captain produced the most prolific campaign of his life, scoring ‌61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions as the German giants completed a domestic league and cup double.
By the end of the season, Kane had established himself as Europe’s leading goalscorer, turning every competition into a showcase of his finishing ability.
